films.name: Tally
films.audience: Freelancers and small studios collecting client enquiries
films.promise: Give the client brief a home.
films.treatment: White paper, dark ink and the product’s blue controls. The same form and the same three answers carry the story. Scattered messages establish the problem; they are never imported into Tally.

shots.title: Recognize the problem
shots.copy: Still taking client briefs in DMs?
shots.framing: A bold question with three surrounding fragments; snap from tight to wide.
shots.subject: The missing client brief
shots.action: Three editorial cards ask What’s your email?, What do you need? and One more thing… around the opening question.
shots.result: The audience recognizes the friction of asking for details one message at a time.
shots.transition: Fragments leave before a clean form arrives. This is an editorial cut, not a DM import.

shots.title: Establish the form
shots.framing: Wide enough to establish the Project enquiry form, then approach its next field.
shots.subject: Project enquiry form
shots.action: The existing name field and project question settle; the email insertion point becomes the next focus.
shots.result: The viewer understands they are building a form.
shots.transition: Move into the same document. Keep the title and existing field recognizable.

shots.title: Make the field tangible
shots.framing: Input close-up with enough context to recognize the form.
shots.subject: Email insertion
shots.action: Type /email, select Email and reveal Your email between the existing name field and What do you need? project question.
shots.result: The added email field completes three questions: name, email and project details.
shots.transition: Retain the form while the view cuts to its Publish control.

shots.title: Commit one clear action
shots.framing: Large, isolated Publish control; a small edge of form context stays visible.
shots.subject: Publish button
shots.action: Pointer approaches, pauses and presses Publish at approximately 7.67–8.07 seconds; the form holds through 10 seconds.
shots.result: A clear editorial handoff to the respondent’s form view after the action has settled.
shots.transition: Cut to the same questions in respondent mode. Do not invent a share modal or send event.

shots.title: Show the actual exchange
shots.framing: Follow each input, then give Submit a distinct close-up.
shots.subject: Ada’s example enquiry
shots.action: Enter Ada, ada@example.com and A new landing page. Press Submit after the values are visible.
shots.result: One respondent has completed all three questions.
shots.transition: Only the Submit action triggers the next confirmation view.

shots.title: Confirm the consequence
shots.framing: Quiet, centered confirmation after the tight action view.
shots.subject: Post-submit confirmation
shots.action: Display the default Thanks for completing this form! state with product branding.
shots.result: The viewer sees that the submission completed.
shots.transition: Move to an explicitly editorial recap, rather than fabricating a Tally dashboard.

shots.title: Let the payoff land
shots.framing: A complete, aligned brief. Settle the camera and hold all three answers.
shots.subject: The same three submitted values
shots.action: An Example brief label introduces three aligned cards containing the previously entered answers.
shots.result: Ada / ada@example.com / A new landing page remain unchanged.
shots.transition: The editorial recap leaves before the final action; do not duplicate or replace its answers.

shots.title: Make the next step specific
shots.framing: Large product name, one action and tally.so. Hold through the final frame.
shots.subject: Create a free form
shots.action: A short directional reveal settles into the offer and destination.
shots.result: The viewer knows what to create and where to start.
shots.transition: Clean end hold. No extra claim or new feature.

steps.title: Define the quality benchmark
steps.detail: Eight reference films inspected; selected mechanisms and their purpose are documented below.

steps.title: Rebuild Tally as the pilot
steps.detail: The approved 24-second authored pilot and matched control passed export checks in all three placements using the shared engine.

steps.title: Plan every shot
steps.detail: The user approved the storyboard before final rendering. Eight views preserve one action/result story.

steps.title: Build stronger camera controls
steps.detail: Source-bound camera targets now distinguish context, input, commit and result, with readable holds and deterministic seeking.

steps.title: Carry objects between views
steps.detail: Matching subjects retain their identity and values. State changes and replacement results are checked for resets and ghost objects.

steps.title: Separate animation layers
steps.detail: Camera, cursor, copy, product state and materials have independent timing on the same frame clock.

steps.title: Create reusable visual styles
steps.detail: Reusable brand-based materials and layouts are implemented. Tally retains paper, ink and observed blue controls; its font uses a fallback. Richer media treatments still need source assets and review.

steps.title: Connect URL generation
steps.detail: Guide capture, source-bound UI reconstruction and explicit action/outcome review are implemented. Research syntax, source context and final quality checks remain under fresh automatic testing. No automatic video has passed.

steps.title: Compose all three placements
steps.detail: Six verified 24-second exports: the new director and matched control, each composed separately for 16:9, 4:5 and 9:16.

steps.title: Review and refine the pilot
steps.detail: Export, frame, layout and muted visual checks passed. Five unfamiliar viewer responses and subjective listening review remain outstanding.

steps.title: Prove it generalizes
steps.detail: Zero automatic passes. Baserow and Resend have produced retained drafts, but final quality checks rejected them. Camera framing and early action are being corrected. The six approved authored Tally exports remain available and do not count as automatic URL passes.

steps.title: Publish and test performance
steps.detail: The gallery includes matched variants and a viewer test. Audience performance remains unmeasured; agree a paid-test budget before buying traffic.

benchmarks.name: ClickUp
benchmarks.purpose: Several framings make one interaction feel cinematic without losing the query.

benchmarks.name: Commas
benchmarks.technique: An offer becomes checkout and confirmation
benchmarks.purpose: The viewer can trace one object through action and consequence.

benchmarks.name: SOVRA FM
benchmarks.purpose: A clear state change earns the result reveal while preserving the brand palette.

benchmarks.name: CraftedStays
benchmarks.technique: Approach the assistant, then reveal the result
benchmarks.purpose: A familiar subject and independent camera movement connect the workflow.

generalization.title: Plausible
generalization.detail: Fresh research selected a supported row-count demonstration without the earlier timing claim. UI generation merged the source label/count and retained unrelated rows, so validation stopped before scripting or video generation.

generalization.title: Resend
generalization.detail: The earlier 14.4-second draft passed layout, motion and its product-demonstration review; its remaining review exceeded the reservation budget. The latest fresh run stopped on an out-of-range UI color before rendering. No complete automatic pass yet.

generalization.title: Baserow
generalization.detail: The latest test captured dashboard documentation and screenshots, then returned no usable research text within its output allowance. No new UI or video was generated. The earlier rendered draft remains unapproved.
